scoring_rule: best of the two selected files on private, confirmed by the user

slot_1.risk: uses aggregate moments recovered from public RMSLE. The organiser confirmed on 25.08 that calibrating on public is allowed and that the client split is random, so formal-rule risk is retired. Statistical public-overfit risk and unquantified adaptive-selection bias remain.

slot_2.role: low-df hedge against an underpriced public-to-private transfer
slot_2.construction: nonnegative ridge with lambda=0.001 applied once to the frozen current pool containing the admitted decay base 127; no search over constructions was performed after the public response.

break_even_analysis.method: private(r) = fitted_public + degrees_of_freedom * r, where r is the true public-to-private transfer penalty per degree of freedom. Clean files have df = 0 because their public score is already unbiased.

slot_2_rationale.120_hedges_the_unmodelled_risk: 120 reads no public score at all. It is the only candidate that covers adaptive-selection bias, which STRATEGY explicitly records as NOT captured by the df formula. Under best-of-two the hedge is free, so the second slot should cover the risk the model cannot price.
slot_2_rationale.low_df_choice: The selected slot keeps the current measured pool while reducing effective complexity with a frozen nonnegativity constraint.

130+123.note: similar diversity to 120 but 123 is the capped clean insurance, chosen role is second-line

130+122.note: most diversified, but 122 costs about 0.002614 of historical quality, so it stays a severe-shift reserve

reproducibility.result: both scripts rebuilt every target and matched the documented SHA-256 exactly; the scripts raise on mismatch
reproducibility.fix_applied_today: reproduce_frozen_finals.py did not cover 130 at all, because 130 is solved with 127 as the primary probe and 102 demoted to an extra. The competition-primary was therefore not reproducible by the documented command. Fixed and re-verified.

slot_2_replaces.why_changed: A scenario table over the true transfer rate r showed that 120 gains NOTHING until r exceeds about 4x our empirical estimate, while a low-df sibling gains from about 1.7x onward. 120 only becomes the counting file when the ensemble is already around 1.6494, i.e. in a world where top-5 is lost anyway, so it limits damage rather than protecting the stated goal. The low-df hedge instead pays off exactly in the band where top-5 is decided, where 4th and 5th on public differed by 3e-06.
slot_2_replaces.adaptive_bias_argument_quantified: 120 is the only candidate immune to adaptive-selection bias b, which the df formula does not price. But 120 only overtakes 130 once b reaches about 0.0024, whereas the project's own accounting charges 0.00004 per admitted base for exactly this effect, giving b of roughly 0.00028 across seven admitted bases. The hedge therefore covers a scenario about eight times larger than our own estimate of it.
slot_2_replaces.supporting_evidence_that_b_is_small: On 26.08 the offline 96-split audit predicted the sw28 public gain as +0.00010687 before submission and the leaderboard returned +0.00011250, agreeing to 5.6e-06. Heavily selection-contaminated moments would not reproduce that accuracy.
slot_2_replaces.residual_risk_accepted: 147 shares the measured pool and the full probe history with 130, so it does not hedge a structural failure of the recovered-moment mechanism. That exposure is accepted deliberately in exchange for covering the far likelier moderate-error band.
slot_2_replaces.prediction_check: Recorded before submission: a public prediction error above 0.0001 would invalidate the candidate. Actual deviation was 1.27e-05, i.e. 8x inside the threshold, so 147 stands.
